# Design & Slide Aesthetics

Visual design principles for presentations that look professional and communicate clearly.

## Color

### The 60-30-10 Rule
- **60%** Dominant color (usually background)
- **30%** Secondary color (shapes, headers, visual elements)
- **10%** Accent color (highlights, CTAs, key numbers)

### Color Palettes for Professional Presentations

| Palette Name   | Dominant       | Secondary      | Accent         | Best For              |
|----- -- -----|-- ----- ------|-- ----- ------|-- ----- ------|--- ---- ---- ------|
| **Midnight**   | `#1E2761` navy  | `#CADCFC` ice  | `#FFFFFF` white| Executive pitches    |
| **Forest**     | `#2C5F2D` forest| `#97BC62` moss | `#F5F5F5` cream| Sustainability, health|
| **Coral**      | `#F96167` coral| `#F9E795` gold | `#2F3C7E` navy | Energetic, creative   |
| **Charcoal**   | `#36454F` charcoal | `#F2F2F2` off-white | `#212121` black | Minimal, premium     |
| **Teal**       | `#028090` teal | `#00A896` seafoam | `#02C39A` mint | Tech, innovation      |
| **Berry**      | `#6D2E46` berry| `#A26769` rose | `#ECE2D0` cream| Luxury, lifestyle     |
| **Azure**      | `#0078D4` blue | `#DEECFF` light | `#106EBE` dark | Corporate, Microsoft  |

### Color Accessibility
- **Contrast ratio** of at least 4.5:1 for text on backgrounds
- **Never** use red/green together to convey meaning (colorblind-safe)
- **Dark text on light backgrounds** reads faster than the reverse

## Typography

### Font Pairing Rules
- **One font** for body, **one** for headers (max two fonts)
- **Sans-serif** for slides (cleaner at distance): Inter, Roboto, Helvetica, Segoe UI
- **Serif** for executive/deck polish: Georgia, Playfair Display, Merriweather

### Font Sizing
| Element          | Minimum Size | Recommended     |
| ----- -- ------ |-- ------ ------|-- ------ ------|
| Title            | 36pt           | 44-60pt          |
| Body text        | 24pt           | 28-32pt          |
| Data labels      | 18pt           | 20-24pt          |
| Footnotes        | 14pt           | 16pt             |

### Typography Rules
- **Never** use more than 2 font weights (regular + one bold)
- **Line height**: 1.3-1.5 for body text
- **Max 6 words per line** for body text on slides
- **ALL CAPS** for headers only — never for body text

## Layout

### The Grid
- **Margins**: At least 1 inch (2.5 cm) on all sides
- **Content zones**: Divide slide into 3 horizontal zones (top: title, middle: content, bottom: footnote)
- **Alignment**: Everything aligns to a column — never "eye-balled"

### Visual Hierarchy
```
1. Title (biggest, boldest)
2. Key visual / image (dominant element)
3. Supporting data (smaller, lighter)
4. Footnote / source (smallest, muted)
```

### White Space
- **More white space = more premium**. Tight slides feel cheap.
- Leave 30% of every slide as "empty" space.
- White space is not wasted — it's a design tool.

## Slide Types & When to Use Them

| Slide Type           | When to Use                | Visual Element          |
| ----- -- ----------- |-- ---- ------ ------ ----- |-- -- -- -- --------- -- |
| **Title slide**      | Opening, section breaks    | Large image + overlay   |
| **Problem**          | Establishing the gap       | Photo + stat            |
| **Solution**         | Introducing the answer     | Diagram / flowchart     |
| **Data/metrics**     | Showing results            | Chart (simple, not complex) |
| **Comparison**       | Before vs. after           | Two-column layout       |
| **Quote/testimonial**| Social proof              | Large text, minimal     |
| **Timeline**         | Roadmap / history           | Horizontal line with dots |
| **Team**             | Credibility                | Photos in a grid        |
| **CTA**              | Close                      | One number + one action  |
| **Thank you**        | End                        | Contact info + QR code  |

## Chart Design Rules

1. **Remove gridlines** — they add noise, not signal.
2. **Label directly** — no legends. Put the label next to the line/bar.
3. **One metric per chart** — if you need two, use two charts.
4. **Color the data, not the decoration** — gray the non-data, color the insight.
5. **Start Y-axis at zero** — unless the variation is tiny, in which case note it clearly.
6. **Title the chart with the takeaway** — "Revenue grew 47% YoY" not "Revenue by Year."

## Image & Icon Rules

- **One image per slide** — if you need two, you're cluttering.
- **Use full-bleed images** with dark/light overlay for text — they're powerful.
- **Icons should be from the same set** — don't mix outline and filled styles.
- **Avoid stock photo clichés** — handshakes, people on phones, "synergy" shots.
